benefits: Uses the Magnus formula, the standard in meteorology.

faqs.a: The temperature at which air becomes saturated and water vapor condenses into dew. When surfaces cool below it overnight, you get morning dew — or fog, or frost.
Because the dew point measures absolute moisture, while relative humidity depends on temperature. A dew point above about 18 C (65 F) feels muggy no matter what the RH says.
faqs.q: Why does dew point matter more than humidity?

faqs.a: Condensation forms on any surface colder than the dew point: cold pipes, windows, and walls. Keep indoor surfaces warmer, ventilate, or run a dehumidifier.
faqs.q: How do I stop condensation on windows?

faqs.a: Roughly: below 10 C feels dry, 10-16 C comfortable, 16-18 C slightly sticky, 18-21 C humid, above 21 C oppressive.
faqs.q: What is a comfortable dew point?

faqs.a: Sustained indoor dew points above about 16-18 C (60-65 F) let mold grow on cool surfaces. Ventilate bathrooms and kitchens and keep indoor RH under 60%.

dew-point-calculator.formula:
Magnus formula (b = 17.625, c = 243.04):
y = ln(RH/100) + (b x T) / (c + T)
dew point = (c x y) / (b - y)   [T in Celsius]
howTo: Enter the relative humidity as a percentage.
Read the dew point and the comfort rating.
Compare surfaces in your home against the dew point to spot condensation risk.
keyFacts: Dew point is the temperature at which air saturates and water condenses.
It measures absolute moisture, unlike relative humidity.
High dew points (above ~18 C) feel muggy and sticky.
Condensation forms on surfaces colder than the dew point.
Indoor dew points above ~16 C encourage mold on cool surfaces.
The Magnus formula is accurate within about 0.5 C for normal weather.

dew-point-calculator.quickAnswer: Enter the air temperature and relative humidity, and this calculator returns the dew point using the Magnus formula — the same equation meteorologists use — plus a comfort rating from dry to oppressive. It works in Celsius or Fahrenheit.
dew-point-calculator.tagline: When will the air give up its moisture?
dew-point-calculator.workedExample:
Air at 25 C with 60% relative humidity:

1. y = ln(0.60) + (17.625 x 25) / (243.04 + 25) = -0.5108 + 1.6438 = 1.1329.
2. Dew point = (243.04 x 1.1329) / (17.625 - 1.1329) = 275.35 / 16.493 = 16.7 C (62.1 F).
3. Comfort rating: 16.7 C falls in the slightly-humid band.

Any surface colder than 16.7 C — a cold drink, an AC vent — will collect condensation.
